new_statements.translation: [p.163] Three regions can be distinguished: the middle region whose Monja/Ewango speech is accepted as the Otetela norm; the right-hand region, between the Lomami and the Lualaba, where the Kusu dialect is spoken; the left-hand region ... where Ohendo/Indanga or Nkutshu is spoken. [p.171] 9. Only one mora (quantity) on radical vowels ... COMMENTARY: In Otetela there are a few cases of long vowels, but this always seems to be through consonant elision and vowel assimilation ... 10. Intensity accent (stress) on the radical syllable (likewise in Zone B). 11. Lexical tone on the radical as well as on the suffixes.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Guthrie's Zone C generalisation, reproduced by the Otetela grammarian Labaere without objection for the Tetela group (of which he names Kusu as the eastern dialect): dynamic stress falls on the radical (stem-initial) syllable; the language is otherwise tonal (two level tones, H and L, per Jacobs 1962 for 'Tetela-Kusu').
new_statements.exceptions: None; Labaere adds no Otetela- or Kusu-specific comment to item 10 (he does comment on items 9, 12, 13 and corrects Guthrie on other points).
new_statements.domain_note: Zone-level typological statement (Guthrie 1948, Zone C 'caracteristiques communes'), transmitted second-hand; applied to Otetela C71 with Kusu treated as its eastern dialect region. No Kusu-specific first-hand statement on stress was found in any opened source; Jacobs 1962 (first-hand, 'Tetela-Kusu') describes tone only and is silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Every accessible source treats Kusu (C72, kusu1252) as the eastern, Maniema part of the Tetela continuum (tete1250): Jacobs 1962 p.31 'Het Tetela, ook Kusu genaamd ten oosten van de Lomami' (area incl. Kibombo, SW Kindu, Mweho in Kasongo, Lubunda in Kongolo) but his tone description rests on the Tshumbe/Wembo-Nyama C71 dialects; Motingea 1989: 'le Nkutsu de Kindu est indiscutablement un dialecte tetela' (87.67% cognate); Labaere & Shango 1989 file the Akusu of Lubefu/Kibombo under the Odya dialect; Labaere 2001 calls it 'le dialecte kusu' of Otetela. The quoted stress statement is Guthrie's Zone C generalisation applied to Otetela C71, not a Kusu-specific observation. False friends excluded: Bukusu (Luhya, Kenya; Austen 1974-75 IU thesis printed as 'Bakusu' in AA 14), Yakusu (BMS station, Lokele), Basankusu (Equateur town).

sources.note: p.163 names 'le dialecte kusu' (between Lomami and Lualaba) as the eastern region of the Otetela area. p.171 reproduces Guthrie 1948's Zone C common feature '10. Accent d'intensite sur la syllabe du radical (Ainsi en Zone B.)' without any Otetela-specific comment (Labaere comments on items 9, 12, 13 and corrects Guthrie elsewhere, but lets item 10 stand). Zone-level, second-hand (Guthrie) statement; not Kusu-specific.

sources.note: Tone description only. p.31 defines the object as Tetela 'ook Kusu genaamd ten oosten van de Lomami', area explicitly including gewest Kibombo and SW Kindu (the Kusu area), but the description is based on the Tshumbe/Wembo-Nyama (C71) dialects. p.32: 'Het Tetela beschikt over twee tonemen: een gelijkmatig hoog en een gelijkmatig laag toneem'; p.42: tone has lexical, grammatical and syntactic function. No word on stress/accent (no 'klemtoon', 'accent', 'nadruk' anywhere in pp.31-42).
